answer: Each agent can earn influence only by staking a scarce token and keeping it locked while its claims are evaluated. A beacon announces the stake and links it to a persistent history; peers challenge inconsistent reports, and slashed collateral pays those who prove fraud. This makes a plume of fresh identities no shortcut to control: the attacker must buy and lock substantial capital for every sybil, risking forfeiture, while honest agents can build influence through a smaller kernel of durable, verifiable work.
